subject: Uptime budget & provisional monthly credit proposal — Brightline
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@brightline.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Initial SLA template + proposed monthly credit structure

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, I’m attaching a draft SLA template and a simple credit matrix that maps uptime buckets to monthly service credit (PDF + spreadsheet attached). High-level proposal:

- Standard availability target: 99.8% monthly (measured at region level)
- Maintenance carveout: scheduled maintenance windows up to 6 hours/month (no credit)
- Provisional monthly credit cap: 12% of monthly invoice for first 6 months of the contract (pilot phase)
- Latency SLO: p95 < 250ms for API inference in our us-west region; separate remediation conversation if not met

We included a provisional cap to give Brightline predictability while we tune batched workloads and KV cache settings — we expect that to materially reduce incidents tied to burst windows. Could you review and let me know any must-haves or immediate concerns? If you prefer, we can propose a smaller cap (e.g., 8%) in exchange for a 100.0% SLA for scheduled maintenance notice windows.

Next steps I’m proposing:
1) You confirm whether the 99.8% target is acceptable as a baseline
2) Brightline indicates a preferred credit cap (provisional) or asks for a different carveout
3) If agreed, we’ll circulate redlines and prepare DocuSign

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if that helps.

—
Karthik Iyer
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0124

Attachment: sla-proposal-v1.pdf (SLA template draft)
Attachment: uptime-credit-matrix.xlsx (credit bands and example calculation)
From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@brightline.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Morales <elena.morales@brightline.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial SLA template + proposed monthly credit structure

Karthik —

Thanks for sending this over and for the clear summary. A few points from our side:

1) 99.8% baseline is in the right direction, but given Brightline’s latency-sensitive workflows at peak traffic we were hoping for 99.9% for the us-west region. Is that achievable without significant price premium?
2) The provisional cap is helpful, but 12% is higher than our procurement team is comfortable with for a pilot — they asked whether we can cap at 6% for the first 3 months and then reevaluate.
3) Maintenance carveouts: we need a minimum of 72 hours advance notice for any maintenance that will affect production traffic routing. Short-notice maintenance is a major risk for our weekend release windows.

If we can meet in the middle on uptime (99.85%) and adopt a stepped cap — 6% for months 1–3, 9% for months 4–6 — we’d be in a position to move forward quickly. We can also share a short intake form that spells out our peak windows so you can consider additional capacity guarantees.

Happy to take a quick 30-min sync this afternoon if you have time.

Thanks,
Sam
Director of Platform Engineering
Brightline Systems
sam.patel@brightline.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@brightline.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 13:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial SLA template + proposed monthly credit structure

Sam —

Appreciate the detailed feedback. Looping in Marissa (Sales Ops) and Laura (Legal) to confirm what we can flex on quickly and to ensure we capture the stepped cap cleanly in the contract language. Connor from Product is on copy to assess the operational ask about 99.85%/99.9% and the 72-hour maintenance notice.

Quick internal notes for the group:
- 99.85% is likely a reasonable compromise for the us-west region if Brightline accepts a structured 30-day monitoring & tuning period post-commencement (we use that period to apply batching/kv-cache profiles specific to their request patterns).
- We can accept a stepped provisional credit cap of 6% (months 1–3) and 9% (months 4–6) conditional on a mutual action plan where Brightline provides peak-window telemetry and keys for a pilot performance evaluation.
- Maintenance notice: 72 hours is acceptable for planned network-impacting maintenance; we’ll retain emergency maintenance carveouts but will provide same-day escalation and rollback guarantees for those events.

Laura — can you draft the redline that reflects the stepped cap and the 72-hour notice as an explicit maintenance carveout? Marissa — once legal confirms wording, can you prepare the updated credit-matrix attachment with the stepped caps and an example invoice calculation?

Sam — if that aligns with you I’ll turn this into a redline and send the DocuSign bundle by EOD.

Best,
Karthik
From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@brightline.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Morales <elena.morales@brightline.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial SLA template + proposed monthly credit structure

Thanks — that sounds workable. Two quick clarifications before you finalize:

• Can we get an explicit example row in the spreadsheet showing how credits would be calculated for a $120k monthly bill at 99.7% vs 99.85%? That helps our finance reviewers.
• For emergency maintenance carveouts, can you define "same-day escalation" (we’d prefer SLA on incident acknowledgement + a rollback window) — e.g., 30-minute ack, rollback within 4 hours where feasible.

If you can include those items in the redline, we’ll route to procurement this afternoon and try to return a countersigned DocuSign by Monday.

Sam
